thread:
maya: Drafting an RFC for hybrid VPC/on-prem egress options — sharing high-level scope and acceptance criteria. looking for quick alignment before i spin into full PRD.

maya: customer asks: private deployment where customer controls egress (must not route customer traffic through our NAT unless explicitly allowed), but wants a fail-open fallback to hosted egress for emergencies.

ryan: question: when you say 'fail-open' do you mean automatic fallback to Redwood-managed egress, or manual switchover?

maya: prefer automatic with explicit policy toggle per-customer. fallback should be rate-limited and audited.

ankit: two implementation paths: 1) customer-managed BGP advertised prefixes -> our edge accepts and routes out directly (bgp handoff), 2) customer uses egress NAT gateway we manage but with customer-owned IPs (hairpin/proxy). each has tradeoffs.

ankit: BGP pros: single-hop, lower latency, no double-nat. cons: requires customer ASNs, config windows, troubleshooting ops.

ankit: managed-nat pros: simpler for customers without bgp. cons: we see egress traffic, increased compliance surface.

{sophie}: compliance note: if we handle egress even briefly, we need logging retention & C2 controls. some customers (regulated) will refuse any egress-in-through-Redwood. we must offer a strict "no-egress-through-redwood" mode.

jordan: prioritization: three customers pushing this (healthcare, fintech, gov). fintech wants strict audit trails + can accept bgp. healthcare needs controlled fail-open but strict logging. gov requires no redwood-egress at all.

maya: acceptance criteria proposal: 
- "no-egress" mode: zero traffic through Redwood-managed egress, validated via packet path tests + automated audit.
- "bgp-handoff" mode: support full BGP peering with customer ASN, support route validation (RPKI optional), and documented handoff playbook.
- "managed-egress" mode: Redwood NAT with customer-owned IPs optionally, must support per-route policy and per-token billing tags.
- failover: automatic failover allowed only when customer has opted in; failover events emit audit records + webhook notification.

maya: added edge cases in draft: overlapping CIDRs, asymmetric return path, MTU fragmentation, path MTU discovery failures, multi-homed customers, route flapping during cutover.

ryan: ops constraints: we need sanity checks pre-cutover: i.e., route leak detection, AS path validation, ack windows for BGP change. also, an automated rollback trigger if more than X% error rate in first 10 minutes.

ankit: config snippet I'm proposing for bgp handoff (customer side):

```
neighbor 203.0.113.5 remote-as 64512
neighbor 203.0.113.5 ebgp-multihop 2
neighbor 203.0.113.5 password <REDACTED>
network 198.51.100.0/24
```

ankit: note: we'll provide templated configs for popular vendors (Cisco, Juniper, Arista) and a validation script that runs from our side before flipping routes.

{tariq}: sales/context: customers expect a clear SLA for route activation time and a checklist for customer network teams. they also want sample legal language about "no persistence of customer payload" when managed-egress is used.

{sophie}: add: encrypted logging (KMS) + redact headers with PII by default. need to list what we store and retention windows in the PRD.

ops-oncall: monitoring/alerting: require per-customer egress telemetry, BGP session state alerts, RPKI validation failures, and jitter/latency SLO infra. we must add synthetic tests that traverse the customer's path and verify return route.

jordan: tradeoff conversation for product: minimum viable launch (MVP) to unblock customers: support bgp-handoff + strict no-egress option. postpone managed-egress for later phase unless a large customer pays for it.

maya: timeline suggestion: 
- RFC review & ops playbook: 2 weeks
- prototyping BGP validation tooling & templated configs: 3 weeks
- 1 pilot customer cutover window after sign-off (customer-managed): 1 week

maya: rollout gates: 
1) test bench: successful synthetic end-to-end with at least 2 different cloud vendors and at least one on-prem firewall appliance.
2) runbook & rollback verified with oncall.
3) documentation + legal checkbox for customers.

ryan: one more risk: asymmetric IP fragments when going through middleboxes. recommend adding MTU tests and explicit MSS clamping guidance to templated configs.

ankit: agree. also add a troubleshooting checklist for NAT hairpin scenarios (if we ever enable managed-egress).

maya: can folks +1 the acceptance criteria and gates or flag objections? i'd like to turn this into a PRD by EOW.

ryan: +1 ops gating, add rollback thresholds (e.g., 5% error spike => auto-rollback).

ankit: +1 for bgp-first MVP. will draft vendor templates and validation script.

{sophie}: +1 for criteria, will provide compliance section for PRD (logging, KMS, redact).

jordan: +1 to MVP plan, product will prioritize pilot customers accordingly.

{tariq}: +1, sales will prep customer-facing one-pager and legal ask list.

deploy-bot: deploy checklist created: `deploy checklist: bgp-handoff-playbook.md, e2e-synthetics, kms-keys-ok, legal-signoff` :white_check_mark:

ops-oncall: noted. i'll book a tabletop drill for rollback playbook next Tue.

maya: awesome, i'll update the RFC with these edits and PRD skeleton. ping me for review once i submit — aiming EOW.

maya: attaching quick link to draft: https://redwood-internal/notes/onprem-egress-rfc (draft)

ryan: thanks — will review this afternoon.

maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
